14: # Create Skill Router
15: 
16: The machine router for [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md). `SKILL.md` keeps the short routing prose and the
17: link that points here; this file holds the declaration a reader parses to decide what loads.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
24: what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
25: loads before an intent selects it.
26: 
27: Requests reach this packet when they ask to create or rebuild an OpenCode skill under `.skilled/skills/`, to run `/create:skill` for a standalone skill or `/create:skill-parent` for a parent hub, to author or repair a skill package's `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/` or `changelog/`, or to validate and package a skill with `scripts/package_skill.py`. Its vocabulary is `create skill`, `new skill`, `skill scaffold`, `SKILL.md scaffold`, `OpenCode skill`, `parent hub`, `mode packet`, `nested workflow packet` and `package skill`. It routes to two resource families: the `references/shared/` doctrine and its root-metadata contract, which both modes load first, and the mode's own `references/<key>/` plus `assets/<key>/` trees, where `create-skill` resolves the `skill` key and `create-skill-parent` resolves `parent-skill`.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
32: 
33: - **`SKILL_PACKAGE`** fires on `create skill`, `/create:skill`, `new skill`, `skill scaffold`, `SKILL.md scaffold`, `OpenCode skill`, `sk-skill`, `create sk-`, `reusable capability`, `reusable helper`, `starter reference docs` and `package skill` at weight 4. It loads the five shared docs — `references/shared/overview.md`, `references/shared/common-pitfalls.md`, `references/shared/validation-and-packaging.md`, `references/shared/advisor-index-handoff.md`, `references/shared/skill-root-metadata-contract.md` — then `references/skill/creation-workflow.md`, `references/skill/examples-and-maintenance.md`, `references/skill/upgrading-a-skill-to-v4.md`, and the nine `assets/skill/` templates: `assets/skill/skill-md-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-readme-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-reference-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-asset-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-procedure-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-scaffold-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-smart-router.md`, `assets/skill/skill-router-template.md`, `assets/skill/skill-sync-manifest-template.md`.
34: - **`PARENT_HUB`** fires on `/create:skill-parent`, `parent skill`, `parent hub`, `mode packet`, `nested workflow packet`, `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` at weight 4. It loads the same five shared docs, then `references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md`, `references/parent-skill/parent-hub-router-schema.md`, `references/parent-skill/compiled-routing-architecture.md`, and the five `assets/parent-skill/` templates: `assets/parent-skill/parent-skill-hub-template.md`, `assets/parent-skill/parent-skill-readme-template.md`, `assets/parent-skill/parent-skill-root-router-template.md`, `assets/parent-skill/scaffold/hub-skill-scaffold.md`, `assets/parent-skill/scaffold/packet-skill-scaffold.md`.
35: 
36: ---

38: ## 3. MACHINE ROUTER
39:

41: reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.

## 2. SMART ROUTING

`hub-router.json` scores the request and selects a `workflowMode`.
`mode-registry.json` maps that mode to its packet.
The root [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) selects the first resources the packet loads.
`packetKind` identifies each packet as `workflow`, `surface` or `transport`.
`routerPolicy` defines the available outcomes.
It returns `single` when one workflow mode wins.
It returns `orderedBundle` when several workflow modes match.
It returns `surfaceBundle` for one workflow mode with read-only surfaces.
It returns `defer` when modes tie or conflict.
Ask which mode the reader means when the router returns `defer`.
When no mode matches, return `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK`.
You run the compiled-routing directive in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) first.

---

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

### Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `[parent-skill-name]/SKILL.md` | Hub instructions |
| `[parent-skill-name]/mode-registry.json` | Packet registry |
| `[parent-skill-name]/hub-router.json` | Routing policy |
| `[parent-skill-name]/ROUTER.md` | Stage-two control document and the hub's routing prose |
| `[parent-skill-name]/description.json` | Hub-doctor metadata |
| `[parent-skill-name]/graph-metadata.json` | Hub identity |
| `[parent-skill-name]/command-metadata.json` | Optional command metadata |
| `[parent-skill-name]/leaf-manifest.json` | Generated leaf inventory |
| `[parent-skill-name]/changelog/` | Hub changelogs |
| `[parent-skill-name]/manual-testing-playbook/` | Manual test cases |
| `[parent-skill-name]/benchmark/` | Benchmark baseline (parent-skill-check 9b warns if absent) |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/SKILL.md` | Workflow instructions |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/README.md` | Workflow overview |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/changelog/` | Workflow changelogs |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/SKILL.md` | Surface instructions |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/README.md` | Surface overview |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/references/` | Surface evidence |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/assets/` | Surface assets |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/changelog/` | Surface changelogs |

### Companion Metadata

- `mode-registry.json` owns `workflowMode`, `packetKind`, `backendKind`, `toolSurface`, packet folder identity, alias phrases, and `advisorRouting`.
- `hub-router.json` owns `routerPolicy`, `routerSignals`, `vocabularyClasses`, and bundle rules.
- `ROUTER.md` is the stage-two control document: `router_state: active` declares non-empty equal-key `INTENT_SIGNALS`/`RESOURCE_MAP`, while `router_state: stage1-only` keeps all stage-two collections empty and delegates to stage one. Promote to `active` only after authoring concrete, resolvable leaf paths, never placeholder intents. Its final `## MACHINE ROUTER` section holds the compiled-routing directive and the fallback checklist, so the hub `SKILL.md` never repeats them.
- `description.json` owns hub-doctor metadata fields and optional hub-specific arrays.
- `graph-metadata.json` owns the one skill-graph identity node.

### Optional Extensions

Use top-level `extensions` in `mode-registry.json` only when the hub needs extra machinery:

- `runtime-loop`: activates per-mode `runtimeLoopType` and convergence backend fields.
- `advisor-projection`: declares the drift-guard path for lexical or alias-fold routes.
- `transform-verbs`: declares verb-transform routing for design-like hubs.
- `deprecated-modes`: documents retired modes kept as shims.
- `surface-axis`: declares that the hub includes `packetKind: "surface"` packets.

**After initialization**: Customize or remove generated files as needed.

# Create skill in .skilled/skills/ directory
scripts/init_skill.py markdown-optimizer --path .skilled/skill

`hub-router.json` scores the request and selects a `workflowMode`.
`mode-registry.json` maps that mode to its packet.
The root [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) selects the first resources the packet loads.
`packetKind` identifies each packet as `workflow`, `surface` or `transport`.
`routerPolicy` defines the available outcomes.
It returns `single` when one workflow mode wins.
It returns `orderedBundle` when several workflow modes match.
It returns `surfaceBundle` for one workflow mode with read-only surfaces.
It returns `defer` when modes tie or conflict.
Ask which mode the reader means when the router returns `defer`.
When no mode matches, return `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK`.
You run the compiled-routing directive in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) first.

|---|---|
| `[parent-skill-name]/SKILL.md` | Hub instructions |

| `[parent-skill-name]/manual-testing-playbook/` | Manual test cases |
| `[parent-skill-name]/benchmark/` | Benchmark baseline (parent-skill-check 9b warns if absent) |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/SKILL.md` | Workflow instructions |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/README.md` | Workflow overview |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[workflow-packet-a]/changelog/` | Workflow changelogs |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/SKILL.md` | Surface instructions |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/README.md` | Surface overview |

| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/assets/` | Surface assets |
| `[parent-skill-name]/[surface-name]/changelog/` | Surface changelogs |

### Companion Metadata

- `mode-registry.json` owns `workflowMode`, `packetKind`, `backendKind`, `toolSurface`, packet folder identity, alias phrases, and `advisorRouting`.
- `hub-router.json` owns `routerPolicy`, `routerSignals`, `vocabularyClasses`, and bundle rules.
- `ROUTER.md` is the stage-two control document: `router_state: active` declares non-empty equal-key `INTENT_SIGNALS`/`RESOURCE_MAP`, while `router_state: stage1-only` keeps all stage-two collections empty and delegates to stage one. Promote to `active` only after authoring concrete, resolvable leaf paths, never placeholder intents. Its final `## MACHINE ROUTER` section holds the compiled-routing directive and the fallback checklist, so the hub `SKILL.md` never repeats them.
- `description.json` owns hub-doctor metadata fields and optional hub-specific arrays.
- `graph-metadata.json` owns the one skill-graph identity node.

### Optional Extensions

Use top-level `extensions` in `mode-registry.json` only when the hub needs extra machinery:

- `runtime-loop`: activates per-mode `runtimeLoopType` and convergence backend fields.
- `advisor-projection`: declares the drift-guard path for lexical or alias-fold routes.
- `transform-verbs`: declares verb-transform routing for design-like hubs.
- `deprecated-modes`: documents retired modes kept as shims.
- `surface-axis`: declares that the hub includes `packetKind: "surface"` packets.

**After initialization**: Customize or remove generated files as needed.

=== val-pack 40-65
## 2. VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS

### Completion Gate (validate_skill_package.py)

**Purpose**: Authoritative pre-completion gate. Run before claiming a skill is done. It delegates the package check, detects standalone versus parent roots from the coupled registry/router declaration, and fails an unclassified root rather than guessing its class.

```bash
scripts/validate_skill_package.py <path/to/skill>
```

### Package Check (package_skill.py --check)

**Purpose**: The package validator the completion gate delegates to. Run it directly when you want the package checks without the standalone-versus-parent classification.

```bash
scripts/package_skill.py <path/to/skill> --check
```

`--check` validates without packaging. It hard-fails on:
- A missing required SKILL.md field (`name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`, `version` — all four).
- A `version` that is not 4-part `X.Y.Z.W`.
- A `name` that does not match the skill folder name.
- A missing required SKILL.md section (e.g., `REFERENCES` with no approved combined-heading variant).

It reports non-kebab generated package paths as advisory findings so existing repository debt remains inspectable. Run `--strict` for a newly generated package: strict validation and actual packaging reject every non-exempt path that is not kebab-case. Python filenames, Python import-package directories, frozen/generated subtrees, and tool-mandated names such as `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `.utcp_config.json`, `action.yml`, and `conftest.py` remain exact.

=== val-pack 128-160
**Purpose**: Full quality assurance for production-ready skills.

**What “comprehensive validation” means in this repo**:

- **Structure checklist (script)**: Deterministic checks from `extract_structure.py` (frontmatter, headings, required sections, fenced code blocks).
- **Render checks (script)**: The deterministic half of content quality. `validate_document.py --json` reports `render_*` warnings for a compound overview heading, an overview that opens without orientation, a joined bold label, a setext underline, a bare URL, a repeated sentence or label, a letter-suffixed H2 number, a related section that is not last, and an intro that restates the Purpose.
- **Content quality (AI)**: Judgement based on the extracted JSON + the actual text (clarity, completeness, examples) and on the questions no check answers: whether the intro and the Purpose differ, whether a governing decision precedes the steps it governs, whether an index lists every file of the directory it indexes, whether a status token leaked into the body, and whether a paragraph packs several mechanisms.
- **Style compliance (AI)**: Judgement against `core-standards.md` (headings format, bullets, emoji rules, consistency).

**Quality gate (qualitative)**:
- **SKILL.md must have zero checklist failures**.
- If content is unclear/incomplete, iterate until the doc is production-ready (no major gaps).

**When to use**: After packaging, before distribution

**Command**:
```bash
scripts/extract_structure.py .skilled/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
# AI evaluates the JSON output and provides quality assessment
```

---

## 3. DISTRIBUTION

### Packaging for Distribution

**Command**:
```bash
scripts/package_skill.py <path/to/skill> <output-directory>
```

**Output**: A zip whose filename and archive root match the hyphenated skill folder name. Packaging runs the strict generated-path check before writing the archive.

## 2. OVERVIEW

### What It Does

create-skill runs one of two workflow modes from a single packet. `create-skill` scaffolds a standalone skill with its own advisor identity, `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/` and `scripts/`, built with `scripts/init_skill.py` and normalized to this repo's section order. `create-skill-parent` scaffolds a parent hub that dispatches to nested workflow or surface packets, with `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` at the hub root and `graph-metadata.json` only there, never inside a nested packet. Both modes end at the same gate: `scripts/validate_skill_package.py` must exit clean before `scripts/package_skill.py` runs. It does not audit or improve an existing skill's prose quality once the skill already exists and only needs review. That is `create-quality-control`.

### Why This Skill Exists

Hand-rolling a new skill from a blank `SKILL.md` means reinventing frontmatter rules, section order, routing pseudocode and validation gates every single time. The drift shows up as skills that skip a required field, use the wrong version format, bury routing logic where the advisor can never find it or miss a validation gate entirely. A parent hub multiplies that risk across a registry, a router and however many nested packets, all of which have to agree with each other or the hub silently misroutes. create-skill exists to scaffold both shapes from vetted templates and then prove the result is valid before anyone calls it done.

### The Two Workflow Modes

| Mode | What the skill scaffolds |
|---|---|
| **`create-skill`** | a standalone skill folder with its own advisor identity, `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/` and `scripts/` |
| **`create-skill-parent`** | a parent hub root with `mode-registry.json`, `hub-router.json`, root `ROUTER.md` (`stage1-only` on a fresh scaffold), `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json` and `command-metadata.json`, plus a `SKILL.md`, `README.md` and `changelog/` per nested packet |
=== README 50-80
**Step 1: Scaffold a standalone skill.**

```bash
# --path is the PARENT directory. init_skill.py creates <path>/my-skill
python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path .skilled/skills
```

`init_skill.py` creates `my-skill/` with `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md` and two prepared trees: a `manual-testing-playbook/` corpus index and a `benchmark/reports/` tree carrying its own run index. `README.md`, `references/`, `assets/` and `scripts/` are added by hand as the skill earns them.

**Step 2: Fill in the real content, then validate.**

```bash
python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/validate_skill_package.py .skilled/skills/<skill-name>
```

Expected output ends with `package_skill.py --check: PASS (exit 0)`.

**Step 3: Package only after validation passes.**

```bash
python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py .skilled/skills/<skill-name> <output-directory>
```

Expected: ✅ Successfully packaged <file-count> files to: <output-directory>/<skill-name>.zip

# Compiled-Routing Architecture For Parent Hubs

The compiled skill router is a closed-cohort, byte-verified fast path that resolves a parent hub's `workflowMode` decision without evaluating the hub's prose smart-router at request time. It exists for exactly the parent hubs that have built and proven a compiled policy against that hub's own legacy routing — no other skill, including any hub `create-skill` scaffolds today, is reachable through it.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

=== 100-115

What this proves: the hub's own router files are internally self-consistent and compile to a stable hash. What it does **not** do:

| | `--compiled-routing ready` | Genuinely `compiled-serving` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine | No shadow-child directory exists yet | Hand-built under `009-parent-hub-rollout/00N-<hub>/`, registered in `HUB_CHILD` |
| Manifest | `servingAuthority: "legacy"`, `shadowOnly: true` | `servingAuthority: "compiled"`, re-minted to the shadow-child hash |
| Coverage proof | None — no scenarios were evaluated | Parity with legacy for the seven admitted hubs; the admission check in Section 4 for a new hub |
| Runtime effect | None; the front door always returns the legacy sentinel for this hub | Live, once the hub also joins `DEFAULT_ON_HUBS` (or the flag is forced on) |
| Owned by | `create-skill` | The hub's own coverage build-out, then the runtime-engine cohort change (Section 5) |

A freshly minted `ready` manifest is inert onboarding evidence — safe, reversible, and inspectable, but it changes nothing at runtime by itself. Treat `compiled-ready (fresh manifest verified)` as "this hub's files are onboarding-clean," never as "this hub now routes compiled traffic." Standalone skills never touch any of this: the manifest concept, the flag, and the front door are all parent-hub-only.

---

=== references/shared/advisor-index-handoff.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

**When to Use**:
- Wiring a create or doctor workflow asset's completion/report section (A5 in `002-core-alignment-fixes/plan.md`)
- Writing a contract test that pins the shared vocabulary across adapters (A6)
- Deciding whether a given create branch renders the full handoff or the narrow leaf-freshness signal only (§6)

**Core Principle**: One vocabulary, not one formatter. Create and doctor are separate prompt-asset workflows with genuinely different result shapes (create reports a scaffold; doctor reports a mutating, phase-gated diagnostic run) — see `research.md` Theme F1/F2 in `035-create-doctor-skill-advisor-alignment/001-research/`. What must stay identical across both is the field names, the metadata-ownership statements, and the verification-state enum below, not the surrounding prose or layout.

> **Advisor refresh is always operator-owned.** No `/create:*` or `/doctor:*` workflow calls `skill_graph_scan` or `advisor_rebuild` as a side effect of scaffolding or diagnosing a skill. Every workflow that touches a skill root reports refresh status as `NOT RUN` and prints the exact command the operator would run — never chains it automatically (research.md Theme B1/B7, "Questions Answered").
>
> The one deliberate rebuild is `/doctor:skill-advisor rebuild`. The operator invokes it to run `advisor_rebuild` and then `skill_graph_scan` behind a backup of `skill-graph.sqlite`. It does not touch a skill root and does not render the handoff below.

---

## 2. METADATA OWNERSHIP

Four files carry advisor-relevant metadata on a skill root. Each has exactly one producer; none is validated against another's vocabulary.

=== references/shared/common-pitfalls.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

This reference catalogs the nine pitfalls that most often degrade a skill: from descriptions that are too vague or too bloated to trigger reliably, through second-person voice and platform-specific assumptions, to YAML mistakes, section placement and a router in the wrong place. Each pitfall pairs a wrong example with the corrected form.

**When to Use**:
- A skill exists but does not trigger when expected
- SKILL.md is straining the context window
- Packaging or budget checks are failing
- Reviewing a freshly authored skill for common defects

**Core Principle**: Most failed skills fail at the description and the section boundaries — fix those first.

> **Note on examples below**: illustrative SKILL.md headings inside the fenced examples are written `\##` (not `##`) so the section-numbering validator — which scans `## N.` lines regardless of code fences — does not count them as this document's own sections. Drop the leading `\` when copying a heading into a real SKILL.md.

---

## 2. COMMON PITFALLS

### Pitfall 1: Generic or Bloated Descriptions
=== references/shared/skill-root-metadata-contract.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

A skill root carries up to nine metadata JSON files. Which of them apply is not a per-skill preference: it follows from the root's **class**, and the class follows from one authored declaration.

**When to Use**:
- Creating a new skill or parent hub and deciding which metadata files to write
- Auditing an existing root, or diagnosing a `ci-skill-root-metadata` failure
- Deciding whether a metadata file may be generated or must be authored

**Core Principle**: Classify first, then check. A root's class is decided by an authored declaration, never by a generated artifact.

> **Not the spec-folder schema.** `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` also exist under `.opencode/specs/` under a completely separate continuity schema. The two are never the same file and never interchangeable. This contract governs `.skilled/skills/<root>/` only, and the gate never scans the spec tree.

---

## 2. THE TWO CLASSES

| Class | What it is | Discriminator |
| --- | --- | --- |
=== references/shared/validation-and-packaging.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

This reference covers the two validation tiers a skill passes before release and the distribution steps that follow. Minimal validation is a fast pre-packaging sanity check; comprehensive validation is a full quality pass before distribution.

**When to Use**:
- Before packaging a skill into a distributable zip
- Before releasing or sharing a skill
- When diagnosing why `package_skill.py` rejected a skill

**Core Principle**: Validate before you package, and package before you distribute.

**Key Sources**:
- `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/quick_validate.py` - minimal frontmatter sanity check
- `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py` - structure checklist for comprehensive validation
- `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/validate_skill_package.py` - completion gate: classifies the root from its registry/router pair (rejecting a half-declared pair as unclassified), runs the parent-hub root checks, and wraps `package_skill.py --check`; standalone class conformance is enforced by the fleet gate `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`
- `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py` - validation plus packaging

---

=== references/skill/creation-workflow.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

This reference is the core create workflow for a skill. It walks the six ordered steps from understanding the skill's purpose through iterating on real usage and includes the SKILL.md authoring questions and the frontmatter completion contract.

**When to Use**:
- Creating a brand new skill from scratch
- Re-scaffolding or substantially rebuilding an existing skill
- Authoring or correcting a skill's SKILL.md sections and frontmatter

**Core Principle**: Build the skill for another AI agent instance to use. Favor information that is beneficial and non-obvious.

**Key Sources**:
- `scripts/init_skill.py` - scaffolds the skill directory
- `scripts/package_skill.py` - validates and packages the skill
- [skill-md-template.md](../../assets/skill/skill-md-template.md) - SKILL.md section pattern
- [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) - frontmatter field rules

---

=== references/skill/examples-and-maintenance.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

This reference pairs worked example skills with the ongoing maintenance workflow. The examples show how anatomy and bundled resources come together for real skill types; the maintenance section covers when and how to update and version a skill.

**When to Use**:
- Looking for a concrete layout to model a new skill on
- Deciding whether an existing skill needs an update
- Choosing a version bump (major/minor/patch) for a skill change

**Core Principle**: A skill is never "done" — model new skills on proven layouts, then iterate from real usage.

**Key Sources**:
- [overview.md](../shared/overview.md) - skill anatomy these examples instantiate
- [creation-workflow.md](./creation-workflow.md) - the create process that produces them

---

## 2. EXAMPLE SKILLS

=== references/skill/upgrading-a-skill-to-v4.md
## 1. OVERVIEW

v4 reshaped `sk-code` into a parent hub: one advisor identity that dispatches to nested workflow-mode packets and read-only surface packets. `sk-git` stayed a single skill. This file is the adopter-facing path for reconciling a customized copy with that split.

**When to Use**:
- You customized `sk-code` or `sk-git` and a framework update now ships a different shape
- You are deciding whether a flat skill should become a parent hub
- You want to keep a customized skill single and avoid a false migration
- You have a single skill in a plain or older Skilled shape, and you want it converted in place so it passes the format gate

**Core Principle**: Convert a skill into a parent hub only when it has two or more distinct jobs. Keep it single when it has one job. You may also drop the repo's parent `sk-code` and keep your own single skill.

**When not to Use**:
- You are creating a brand-new skill from scratch. Use `/create:skill` or `/create:skill-parent` directly. See [creation-workflow.md](creation-workflow.md) and [parent-skills-nested-packets.md](../parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md)
- You are only scoring or editing prose in an existing skill. Use `create-quality-control`
- You are tempted to convert framework-internal skills (`sk-doc`, `system-spec-kit`, `system-deep-loop`, and peers). Leave those alone

**Key Sources**:
- `/create:skill-parent` - parent-hub scaffold (`create` or `update`). Argument order is `<skill-name> [create|update] [--modes <m1,m2,...>] [--surfaces <s1,s2,...>] [--path <dir>]`

Use the parent-hub path when one public skill identity must dispatch to multiple packets.

1. Confirm the hub is one advisor-routable identity, not multiple standalone skills.
2. Keep the hub routing-only; nested packets own detailed workflows, evidence, examples, tool boundaries, and validation.

Add `command-metadata.json` only when the hub owns slash commands; when present, it has one entry per owned command.

   Only then replace `router_state` with `active` and add non-empty equal-key `INTENT_SIGNALS`/`RESOURCE_MAP` whose paths resolve and map to typed `leaf-manifest.json` pairs.

9. Give a workflow packet its own `procedures/` folder, using `assets/skill/skill-procedure-template.md`, when it has multiple distinct, individually-triggered internal processes; use `shared/procedures/` only for a card that genuinely coordinates two or more packets.
